title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
transcript_header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Recording: cloud
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mike Torres (NovaHealth CTO), Sara Nguyen (NovaHealth ML Lead), Javier Morales (NovaHealth Infra), Lena Park (NovaHealth PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood serving performance to the customer baseline provider. Went over latency and throughput numbers, tuning knobs (batch size, quantization profile, KV/prefix caching), and discussed options for Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot. Customer asked about security (SOC2/KMS) and runbook for scale testing. Agreed next steps: share detailed benchmark spreadsheet, run follow-up stress test with larger batch sizes and warm KV cache, schedule security deep-dive next week.
topics:
1) Baseline vs Redwood raw numbers (p50/p95/p99)
2) Throughput scaling and batch configs
3) Quantization/accuracy tradeoffs
4) KV cache and prefix hit impacts
5) Dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback plan
6) Security checklist (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call. We wanted to walk through the benchmark spreadsheet we shared earlier this morning, compare against your baseline provider numbers and surface tuning recommendations.
[00:22] Mike: Yep, all here. Thanks — excited to see numbers. Sara and Javier on the call too.
[00:30] Priya: Quick context — tests ran against the same model family you sent — 6.7B-ish open model, 2k tokens context, mixed prompt sizes. We ran three configs: Redwood hosted default, Redwood with quantized weights (q4f16), and your baseline provider instance.
[01:05] Sara: One thing — in our baseline we had autoscaling spikes that increased p95 a lot, so curious how you simulated load.
[01:18] Jordan: We replayed your traffic trace at 70% and 140% of expected peak to check tail latency. Also ran sustained throughput ramp for 10 minutes to look for degradation.
[01:34] Javier: Can you call out the p95 numbers? The spreadsheet has lots of columns.
[01:40] Priya: Sure — at 70% load with cold start warmup, Redwood default p50: 85ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 320ms. With quantized q4f16 path p50: 75ms, p95: 120ms, p99: 280ms. Your baseline provider measured p50: 180ms, p95: 420ms, p99: 950ms under the same replay.
[02:10] Mike: Wow, that's a big gap on p95. Are those numbers per-token or end-to-end?
[02:18] Priya: End-to-end inference time for a 2k-token generation (we normalized to tokens/sec as well). Redwood throughput sustained at ~380 tokens/sec per GPU in the quantized run; baseline was ~160 tokens/sec. That maps to the latency differences.
[02:45] Sara: How consistent are those numbers across sequence lengths? Our workload varies — short prompts and long ones.
[02:53] Priya: We split tests: short (<=256 tokens) short-run p95 was around 60ms/120ms (Redwood/baseline). For long 2k token runs we saw the deltas I mentioned. The kernel-level optimizations and continuous KV cache give bigger wins as sequences grow.
[03:20] Javier: Any differences in output quality with quantization? We care about hallucination risk.
[03:28] Priya: Good question — we ran the eval runs you provided (ROUGE and your internal prompt set). q4f16 showed <1.2% delta on your QA accuracy metrics vs fp16 baseline. We can share the per-prompt diff file. There are edge cases but overall small.
[03:55] Alex: Also worth calling out batching: increasing max batch size to 12 improved throughput by ~20% but added ~15ms to p50; p95 improved overall because GPU utilization was better. So there's an interesting latency vs cost tradeoff you can tune.
[04:20] Mike: Can you explain KV/prefix cache impact again?
[04:26] Priya: On our runs with a 40% prefix hit rate — common for your conversation flows — p95 dropped 30–40%. If you cache recent prefixes or tokenized contexts, the KV cache avoids recomputing attention for earlier segments. We saw p95 go from 150ms to 100ms in cached scenarios.
[04:55] Sara: Nice. For the pilot we want to test warm cache performance since our UX keeps conversations open.
[05:02] Priya: We'll include a warm-cache stress run in the follow-up.
[05:08] Javier: On infra side, how does Dedicated compare? If we reserve capacity, do we get better tail latencies?
[05:18] Jordan: Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and reduced noisy neighbor effects — in our Dedicated emulation runs p95 improved another ~10–15% vs hosted because of reserved lanes and tuned batching. It also simplifies predictable cost accounting.
[05:33] Mike: Pricing aside, we want predictable SLOs. Our SREs will want audit logs, KMS, SSO. Is all that available for dedicated?
[05:43] Alex: Yes — Redwood Private/Dedicated includes KMS integration, SOC2 controls, and SSO/SAML support. We'll attach the security package doc.
[05:54] Lena: For compliance we also need data residency options and an audit trail for prompts — can you produce session-level logs?
[06:02] Alex: Session-level logs and per-token cost telemetry are part of the Console add-on; can be redacted. We'll share the retention and redaction options.
[06:12] Mike: On the baseline provider, we saw degraded throughput after sustained 8-minute runs; did Redwood show any thermal throttling?
[06:20] Priya: We monitored GPU utilization and thermal metrics — no throttling in our runs. Continuous batching and memory management plus KV caching kept utilization steady. We did a long 20-minute run and throughput held within 5% variance.
[06:40] Javier: Can you rerun with larger batches? We plan bursts where many users send simultaneous asks.
[06:45] Priya: Absolutely — proposed follow-up: a stress run at 2x peak with batch sizes up to 24, and with both cold and warm cache profiles.
[06:55] Sara: Also include a high-variance traffic pattern — bursts and then idle.
[07:01] Priya: We'll add that.
[07:05] Alex: Quick note on safety and accuracy — we saw small degradation on very long contexts with q4; if you have critical prompts we recommend either hybrid routes (fp16 for the critical flows) or rolling quantization with eval monitoring.
[07:20] Mike: Understood. For pilot success criteria — what should we measure?
[07:25] Jordan: Suggested: p95 under expected peak <200ms, token throughput >= 300 tokens/sec per GPU for your mixed workload, and <1.5% accuracy regression vs your baseline on evaluation prompts. Also operational: no throttling during 20-minute sustained run.
[07:45] Lena: Sounds reasonable. Timeline — we'd like to decide Dedicated vs Hosted by end of next week.
[07:52] Alex: Good — we'll aim to get the follow-up runs and the security packet by Wed 2026-03-25.
[08:00] Mike: Can you also share the raw CSVs? Our infra team wants to ingest data into our dashboard.
[08:05] Priya: Yes we'll push the raw CSVs and a summary sheet with visual charts.
[08:12] Javier: A couple of nitty details — what versions of CUDA/cuDNN were used? Our baseline used a specific stack and we want to mirror.
[08:20] Priya: Test rigs ran on CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9, and kernels compiled for Ampere and Hopper — we'll put the exact build matrix in the notes.
[08:34] Sara: Any comments on warm start times for large models? Cold starts are a problem for sporadic traffic.
[08:40] Jordan: Warm start in hosted is typically 6–12s depending on model size; Dedicated startup is quicker when using pinned pools — 1–3s for a warmed replica. We also have a pre-warm option for idle replicas.
[08:58] Mike: Good. On the security call we want to see SOC2 cert and a short threat model for our PII flows.
[09:06] Alex: We'll schedule a security deep-dive next week with our security lead.
[09:12] Lena: Action items then?
[09:15] Alex: Recap — Priya to run stress tests (2x peak, batch up to 24, warm/cold cache) by 2026-03-24; Priya/Jordan to upload raw CSVs and annotated spreadsheet today; Alex to send security packet and SOC2 artifact by 2026-03-25; Redwood to propose Dedicated pilot cost estimate and expected capacity numbers by 2026-03-24.
[09:46] Mike: That works. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[09:50] Alex: None, just need the final traffic trace for the burst pattern — Javier will upload.
[09:58] Javier: Uploading now, will notify.
[10:02] Sara: One last Q — if we see a 2% accuracy drop on production prompts, what's rollback plan?
[10:09] Priya: We support per-route rollbacks, canary and A/B, and automatic fallbacks to baseline provider or fp16 variants. We'll add a suggested rollback playbook in the notes.
[10:25] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the security deep-dive.
[10:32] Mike: Thanks all.
[10:38] [meeting ends]
